descriptionChirho: A feminine noun שַׂעֲרָה denoting a hair or strand of hair, used both for individual hairs (in expressions emphasizing precision or divine care, e.g., 'not a hair shall fall') and collectively for hair as a substance. All three clusters represent the same noun in different inflectional forms: partitive with preposition מִן and construct/suffix (S143144, 3x: eng 'from hair of/of his hair', spa 'de cabello de/de su cabello', hin बाल से, arb مِنْ شَعْرَتِهِ, kor 머리카락에서, swa 'unywele'), definite or construct singular (S143145, 2x: eng 'the hair', spa 'el cabello/cabellos de', hin बाल, arb شَعْرَةُ/الشَّعْرَةِ, kor 털이, swa 'nywele za'), and comparative plural (S143146, 2x: eng 'than the hairs of', spa 'que cabellos de', hin से बालों, arb أكْثَرَ مِنْ شَعْرِ, kor 머리카락들 보다, swa 'kuliko nywele za'). All are grammatical variants of one sense.
